authority: Jordan Standards and Metrology Organization (JSMO)
intro:
The Jordan Standards and Metrology Organization is an independent public government institution established under Law No. 22 of 2000. It is the national body responsible for preparing and adopting standards and technical regulations, organizing measurement systems, and monitoring product quality and safety in Jordan.

It also grants conformity certificates and the Jordan Quality Mark, accredits laboratories, inspection bodies, and certification bodies, monitors markets, protects consumers, and supports the competitiveness of national products.

authority: Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology (MoIAT)
intro: The Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology was established in the United Arab Emirates in July 2020 to empower the national industrial sector and increase its contribution to GDP. To build an integrated national system for supporting and developing UAE industry, the Office of the Minister of State for Advanced Technology, the Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology, and the industry sector of the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure were merged into the ministry, with their authorities and functions transferred to it.

authority: Halal Department - Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture
intro: Bahrain Municipality, now Manama Municipality, was established in July 1919 and was among the first municipalities in the Arab world and the first modern administrative and regulatory body in the Kingdom. It began with core duties such as cleanliness and organization, then expanded to urban planning, infrastructure development, and public services. Over the decades it developed into an integrated ministry managing municipal affairs and supporting sustainable development.

authority: National Institute for Standardization and Industrial Property (INNORPI)
intro: INNORPI is a non-administrative Tunisian public institution under the supervision of the Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mines, established in 1982 under Law No. 38-2009. It prepares the national standards program, grants conformity certificates and national quality marks for products, services, and management systems, and handles patents, trademarks, industrial designs, and models. It also represents Tunisia in international and regional organizations including ISO, IEC, WIPO, AIDMO, ARSO, and EPO.

authority: Ministry of Industry and Pharmaceutical Production - Algerian Institute for Standardization
intro: The national standardization body in Algeria is responsible for preparing and publishing national standards and representing Algeria in Islamic technical committees, including those related to Halal matters.

authority: Djiboutian Agency for Standards and Quality
intro: A national body concerned with standards, quality, and conformity assessment in the Republic of Djibouti.

authority: Saudi Halal Center
intro: The Halal Center at the Saudi Food and Drug Authority provides Halal certification services for establishments, covering food products and service providers. The process begins when an establishment submits a request, after which the center sends the requirements and application form. Once completed, eligibility is assessed, the financial agreement is sent for signature, and an audit visit verifies conformity before an approval or rejection decision is made. Contact: halal@sfda.gov.sa | 19999 | www.sfda.gov.sa

authority: Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO)
intro: SASO works toward global leadership in quality infrastructure to strengthen the Kingdom's competitiveness and quality of life. Its mission is to lead the national quality infrastructure system through effective partnerships, technical expertise, and distinguished services that enhance the competitiveness and quality of products and services. Its values include proficiency, transparency, integration and cooperation, reliability, and innovation.

authority: Syrian Arab Organization for Standardization and Metrology
intro: The national body responsible for preparing and adopting standards and following standardization and conformity affairs.

authority: Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organization
intro: The Sudanese Standards and Metrology Organization is an independent preventive and regulatory body affiliated with the Council of Ministers. It was established by Council of Ministers Resolution No. 287 of 1992, with its formal establishment order issued in 2007. It operates under laws on standards, metrology, measurement, calibration, and precious metals control issued in 2008. It holds ISO 9001 certification from BSI and ISO 17025 certification for 11 laboratories, and is a full member of ISO, IEC, CODEX, AIDMO, ARSO, BIPM, OIML, and other international and regional organizations.

authority: Somali Bureau of Standards
intro: The Somali Bureau of Standards, SoBS, is an independent national body established under the Somali Standards and Quality Control Law Lr27 and has operated officially since 2020. It aims to build an integrated quality infrastructure covering standards, metrology, accreditation, and conformity assessment, protect consumers from harmful and substandard products, support export competitiveness and local production standardization, and join international and regional standards organizations. Through it, the Somali government seeks to ensure the safety of imported products and open foreign markets for local industry to strengthen employment, the trade balance, and the national economy.

authority: Central Organization for Standardization and Quality Control
intro: The Central Organization for Standardization and Quality Control in Iraq is a long-established body founded in 1979 under Law No. 54, with roots extending to the 1960s through the Iraqi Standards and Metrology Authority in 1963, the Industrial Research and Control Directorate in 1973, and related bodies. It aims to strengthen industrial production control, protect the national economy, support international trade exchange, and build consumer confidence in national products. It is linked to the Ministry of Planning and Development Cooperation because of its regulatory and neutral role.

authority: Directorate General for Standards and Metrology
intro: The Sultanate of Oman is a distinctive investment destination in the Gulf region, advancing under Vision 2040 toward sustainable economic diversification. The Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion provides comprehensive support for all types of businesses, from startups and SMEs to multinational companies. Oman is distinguished by world-class infrastructure, a strategic position as a gateway to regional and global markets, a skilled multilingual workforce, and integrated business and industrial centers.

authority: Palestine Standards Institution
intro: The Palestine Standards Institution was established in 1994 by decision of President Yasser Arafat and began operating in 1997 under Law No. 6/2000. It has financial and administrative independence and is the national standards body and point of contact with the global quality infrastructure. It works to strengthen the competitiveness of Palestinian products, facilitate trade, and protect consumers and the environment by preparing Palestinian standards and providing testing, inspection, metrology, and conformity certification services. Its board is chaired by the Minister of National Economy and includes representatives of the public and private sectors and academic institutions.

authority: Qatar General Organization for Standards and Metrology
intro: The authority prepares and adopts Gulf and international Halal standards in Qatar.

authority: Public Authority for Industry
intro: The Public Authority for Industry in Kuwait provides, under Industry Law No. 6 of 1965, a comprehensive set of services for industrial investors. These include facilitating transactions through an integrated service center, providing industrial investment opportunities, developing exports, granting customs exemptions, managing industrial zones, supporting investors financially and technically, participating in industrial exhibitions, providing a comprehensive database on industrial establishments inside and outside Kuwait, and converting transactions to electronic systems to accelerate administrative work, with the aim of developing Kuwaiti industry and strengthening its global competitiveness.

authority: Lebanese Standards Institution
intro: The Lebanese Standards Institution, LIBNOR, is a public institution affiliated with the Ministry of Industry. It was established on July 23, 1962, and has the exclusive right to prepare, publish, and amend national standards, as well as to grant the Lebanese conformity mark NL. Lebanese standards are prepared through specialized technical committees and cover dimensions, symbols, terminology, product quality requirements, testing and analysis methods, and professional and construction practice rules. These standards are voluntary in principle, but may be made mandatory by a decree of the Council of Ministers for reasons related to public health, public safety, or national interest. LIBNOR is also a member of several international and regional organizations, including ISO, AIDMO, the Francophone Standardization Network RNF, SMIIC, and an affiliate member of CEN, and serves as Lebanon's national contact point for the Codex Alimentarius Commission.

authority: National Center for Standardization and Metrology
intro: The Libyan National Center for Standardization and Metrology is the sole national body responsible for preparing and issuing Libyan standards under Law No. 5 of 1990. It operates as a scientific research body concerned with standardization, quality, and calibration to protect consumers and the environment. It supervises mutual recognition agreements for conformity certificates to ensure import quality and support the competitiveness of Libyan exports. It is an active member of ISO, AIDSMO, SMIIC, ARSO, and OIML, and is a contact point for the Codex Alimentarius Commission. It also works to spread a culture of quality and management system standards through conferences, seminars, and workshops.

authority: Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality (EOS)
intro: The Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality is Egypt's sole approved national reference for preparing and issuing standards, quality assurance activities, conformity assessment, testing, and industrial calibration. It aims to raise the competitiveness of Egyptian products, protect consumers and the environment, and represent Egypt in international organizations. It was founded in 1957 by Presidential Decree No. 2 and joined ISO in the same year. Its name evolved through presidential decrees until it reached its current name in 2005, and in 2024 the National Quality Institute, the Chemistry Authority, and central laboratories were merged into it.

authority: IS EG Halal
intro: IS EG Halal is the only body exclusively licensed by the Egyptian government to grant Halal certificates for exports worldwide. It serves companies in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetics sectors that want access to the Egyptian market and the Islamic world. It leads efforts to unify Halal certification standards internationally to ensure clean products free from harmful substances while observing the highest animal welfare standards under Islamic rulings. Certified products include meat, agricultural food products, food additives, nutritional foods, medicines, and personal care products.

authority: Moroccan Institute for Standardization (IMANOR)
intro: The Moroccan Institute for Standardization, IMANOR, is a public institution with legal personality and financial independence, established under Law No. 12-06 on standardization, certification, and accreditation. It operates under the supervision of the ministry responsible for industry, trade, investment, and the digital economy. The institute is managed by a board that includes representatives of ministries, professional organizations, research and training institutions, consumer associations, laboratories, and technical centers. IMANOR seeks to help Moroccan businesses adapt to international standards and market requirements by preparing standards, granting conformity certificates, and providing training and information, strengthening their competitiveness and its position as a trusted partner in standardization and quality.

authority: National Office for Standardization and Metrology (ONANOR)
intro: The National Office for Standardization and Metrology, ONANOR, is Mauritania's national reference body for setting national standards and ensuring conformity and metrology. It operates under the supervision of the Ministry of Mines and Industry and seeks to develop quality infrastructure and strengthen regional and international cooperation in standardization to protect consumers and support the national economy.

authority: Yemen Standardization, Metrology and Quality Control Organization (YSMO)
intro: The Yemen Standardization, Metrology and Quality Control Organization, YSMO, is the sole national body in the Republic of Yemen responsible for preparing and adopting standards, conformity control, and affairs related to jewelry and precious metals, under Law No. 44 of 1999 and Presidential Decree No. 52 of 2000. It aims to protect consumer health and safety and the environment, and to support the national economy by controlling locally produced and imported goods.
